notes: The extract carries no participant identifier; row position is used as a synthetic within-dataset id. ESPAD_Cluster_School and ESPAD_Cluster_Class identify schools and classes, not individuals. Each ESPAD wave is an independent cross-section, so no row can be linked to another.
ESPAD survey wave. Waves are independent cross-sections, not repeated measures on the same students. The tidier keeps 2015 and 2019 only, the waves that asked about screen use.
ESPAD wave year; fieldwork runs in the spring of that year.
No age variable in the extract. ESPAD samples students who turn 16 in the calendar year of the survey and collects in the spring, so 15 is used as the whole-year age for every row.
Single gender item. The Other and rather-not-answer options were added in later waves; rather-not-answer maps to Unknown.
Belgian, Russian and Bosnian sub-national samples collapse to Belgium, Russia and Bosnia and Herzegovina. Every other ESPAD country maps one to one.
Screen use is asked in banded response options. NA before 2015, when no screen use item was asked.

expression:
case_when(
  ESPAD_Year == 2019 ~ "Custom: ESPAD gaming time, school and non-school day",
  ESPAD_Year == 2015 ~ "Custom: ESPAD internet gaming time, typical day",
  .default = NA_character_
)
notes: Bespoke ESPAD items, worded differently in 2015 and 2019. NA before 2015, when no screen use item was asked.
ESPAD is a self-completed classroom questionnaire. NA before 2015, when no screen use item was asked.

Hours playing games on a school day, asked in 2019 only. Bands converted at their midpoint (2-3 h to 2.5, 4-5 h to 4.5); the open top band 6 h+ takes its lower bound, following the convention used for the other cohorts.
Hours playing games on a non-school day, asked in 2019 only. Bands converted as for st_game_wd.

2019 rows use the 5:2 weighted mean of the school and non-school day items. 2015 rows fall back to the single gaming item from the internet-use block, which asks about a typical day in the last 30 days and covers online gaming only. Mixing the narrower 2015 item with the 2019 all-gaming items is the reason this row is partial. Not asked before 2015.

The only social media items are agree/disagree statements about spending too much time and about mood, which measure perceived problematic use rather than time. The preregistration excludes problematic-use-only measures.
The 2015 internet-use block is supplied in this extract for gaming only, so no general internet time can be derived. The gaming items are used in st_game.
